Use ground beef and make your own burger don't buy the ready made frozen shit for starters.

I use a ton of seasoning when cooking the patty. To take it to the extra level I put a slice of cheese between two thin patties so it melts in the center while you cook it. Pieces of chopped onions cooked in it's really good too.
I like to follow Frank Sinatra's recipe, but I substitute the Deano for my buddy Jay.

Start with some good ground beef. Mix in finely diced onion and garlic (or powdered versions) and Worcestershire sauce in addition to your staples like salt and pepper. A bit of raw egg can be good for helping them stick together better too. I'd normally do one egg per pound of beef or so.

Now that your meat is ready, make patties that are about 1/3 lb raw (they'll cook down) and are about half an inch thick. Cook the first side with no lid and flip once the raw/cooked line on the side has gone just past halfway up.

Flip the burger over and put on a thick slice of sharp cheddar (I'm partial to Tillimook). Cover with a lid and check on it after a bit less time than the first side took. You're shooting for getting the beef medium.

Pull them off the heat and go directly to a bun. I like the Dave's Killer Bread version, but it's likely not available where you live. Too bad; it's the best mass produced bread ever.

Top with veggies and condiments of your choice. The correct choices are mustard, a romaine lettuce leaf or two, and a hot house tomato slice.

As with all cooking, don't skimp on the ingredients.

I take ground beef and season with Worcestershire and Texas-style barbecue sauce. Add fine ground cracker to help soak up the sauce and keep the burger somewhat solid. I vary the seasonings. These days I'm experimenting with Moroccan style spices. Keep the patties thin so they're easier to cook and easier to eat. Open flame with charcoal and mesquite is my favorite cooking method, but electric skillet works too. Foreman grills dry the burgers too much.

Aged cheddar works best, imo. Cracker Barrel makes a good one. Slice thin, give it a minute to melt on the burger, and serve on the bun of your choice. These day's I use a Hawaiian sweetbread bun.

Form your own patties, dont pack them too tight or too tall.

Salt and pepper both sides of the patty.

Heat a cast iron skillet on high. Add a dab of butter to grease the pan.

Sear both sides on high heat.

Turn the heat down to medium and put a cover on the skillet. Let it cook throgh for a couple minutes.

Flip the patty once and add your cheese choice. Put cover back and continue until cheese is melted.

Have your bun and whatever toppings ready to go.

Plate your burger.
